text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat over the weekend in an approximate range of $169.60 to $171.22 a tonne FOB, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for October 10-31, they said.

- Surinam bought 2,800 tonnes of U.S. northern spring/dark northern spring wheat under PL 480 export program on September 27, USDA said. Shipment was set for October 10-25. The wheat was acquired from Cargill Inc at $186.09 a tonne, FOB U.S. Gulf.

BARLEY SALE - Saudi Arabia has confirmed it signed deals to buy more than 1.4 million tonnes of barley, the official Saudi Press Agency reported late on Sunday. The barley was bought for import between October and December at prices ranging from $146-$158 per tonne, including c and f.

RICE SALE - Sri Lanka has bought 12,500 tonnes of Indian rice and 12,500 tonnes of Vietnamese rice for October delivery, the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The Indian parboiled rice was bought at $250.40 per tonne for third week October and white raw rice of Vietnamese origin at $238.49 tonnes C&F for delivery in the fourth week of October.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka will seek 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat on October 18. It seeks 50,000 tonnes of soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 is the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDERS - Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold four tenders for a total of 104,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 88,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said. State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp may seek 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans for shipment from the U.S. Gulf from October 25 to November 10.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will soon invite bids for 50,000 tonnes of rice for November/December delivery, officials of the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The new purchase will be for delivery in November and December and there will be no restrictions on rice origin.
MARKET TALK - The USDA authorized $200 million in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. farm goods to Egypt under the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal year 1997.

... China is considering the import of disinfected U.S. wheat grown in areas affected by Tilletia Controversa Kuhn (TCK) smut if U.S. scientists can eliminate the fungus, state media on Sunday quoted an official as saying.

Quarantine officials of the two countries have begun cooperating to find a way to healthier farm produce trade, Liu Congmeng, director general of the Ministry of Agriculture's department of international cooperation, said in the China Daily Business Weekly.
